quote: I my I just got my bill yesterday. It's a $137.
stewart_read: Barbara volunteers her bill amount unprompted, a clean capture moment, but the rep does not use the number to build emotional weight before moving to the kWh graph ask.
alternative_hypothesis: Reactive read: rep was simply following the immediate next script step (kWh graph) and treated the dollar figure as incidental rather than a hook to reflect back.
coaching_implication: Coach the rep to pause on a volunteered dollar figure — even one sentence like reflecting the number back before pivoting to the kWh ask — before moving to the next verify item.

quote: Oh, we don't need it for the price. We need it for the yearly kilowatt usage.
stewart_read: Procedurally the redirect to kWh usage is correct since that is what design requires, but the rep treats the $137 figure as noise to move past rather than as the emotional anchor to flip against the utility later. This is the same underlying moment as 01:10 — the redirect itself is defensible, but the flip opportunity is still missed.
alternative_hypothesis: Strategic read rejected: there is no later moment in the call where the rep circles back to the $137 figure to build urgency or contrast against solar savings, so the omission is not part of a deferred strategy — it is simply dropped.
coaching_implication: This is the flip point the schema calls for — 'ask + acknowledge + flip' — and the rep only executed 'ask + acknowledge + redirect.' Replay this exact line with the rep to show where the flip belongs.

quote: Are you not on a cell phone right now?
stewart_read: Barbara is questioning why the text is coming from a different number than the one the rep is speaking on — a legitimacy/trust check about the mechanics of the call, not about how her contact info was obtained. No populated schema protocol cleanly covers this specific device-legitimacy question; it sits adjacent to protocols.how_did_you_get_my_number but is not the same trigger.
coaching_implication: Flag as a schema gap for Kenny: customers questioning why a text arrives from a second/personal number is a distinct micro-moment from 'how did you get my number' and may need its own scripted reassurance line, especially as this pattern will recur once Stewart's automated bill-capture ships from a dedicated number.

quote: I'm on my work phone right now, but I just texted you off my other phone so I that's the one I can get, like, pictures sent to.
stewart_read: Rep discloses using a personal/other phone to receive the bill photo, the exact anti-pattern the schema flags as a privacy/security exposure risk on the floor.
coaching_implication: Flag this line for the security/privacy review the schema calls for; this rep is a candidate for migration onto an automated bill-capture flow once available.

quote: oh, I just need to find you a good date. Sorry. I'm trying to talk to a specialist to see what we can even do for you.
stewart_read: The rep narrates uncertainty about scheduling logistics directly to the customer, which undercuts the calm, confident framing the schema wants during button-up. It's not technical scope creep but it is process transparency that reduces the customer's confidence in the smoothness of the appointment.
alternative_hypothesis: Reactive read: the rep may have genuinely been checking calendar availability live and simply thought aloud, not a deliberate confidence failure.
coaching_implication: Coach the rep to handle scheduling lookups silently or with a filler line ('bear with me one second') rather than narrating internal uncertainty about whether an appointment slot even exists.

quote: K. I'll text you after this to remind you, and then they'll be over at 10AM on Tuesday. Okay?
stewart_read: The rep confirms day and time and promises a text follow-up, but never states the one-hour block, the no-driving/computer instruction, or gets an explicit 'is that fair?' handshake before the call ends.
coaching_implication: Button-up is incomplete — coach the rep to run the full close checklist (hour block, computer/no-driving ask, explicit fairness handshake) even on short, easy calls where the customer seems compliant.
